name: WoodWing Smart Mover workflow archive and replacement bridge
demand: WoodWing's site reports 1,500+ customers and 100,000+ users across its products, but does not identify how many use Smart Mover; its active installations, workflow count, search demand, and willingness to pay are unverified. Support ended 2026-03-27. The headline EOL is 2027-03-27, but existing customers can continue under the Transition Support Plan through 2029-03-31, so March 2027 is not a universal forced-migration cutoff. Sources: https://www.woodwing.com/ ; https://helpcenter.woodwing.com/hc/en-us/articles/51981569765009-Smart-Mover-Transition-Support-Plan-after-end-of-life
prices: No public price found for this proposed archive/converter or for Smart Mover itself. WoodWing says STSP remains at the customer's existing rate, which is unpublished, and that a WoodWing replacement project can receive up to 12 months of STSP fee credit; it also says replacement is a one-time project and ongoing cost will be higher than Smart Mover, without publishing amounts. Current alternatives: n8n Cloud Starter is €20/month and Pro €50/month when billed annually; its self-hosted Community edition is free, subject to its license. Workato self-service Pro starts at $75/month for 2,500 credits. A reseller lists Enfocus Switch Core Engine plus Metadata at €2,796/year. Sources: https://helpcenter.woodwing.com/hc/en-us/articles/51981569765009-Smart-Mover-Transition-Support-Plan-after-end-of-life ; https://n8n.io/pricing/ ; https://support.n8n.io/article/can-i-use-your-license-for-my-use-case ; https://docs.workato.com/en/pricing/self-service/self-service.html ; https://grafistore.com/en/software-oplossingen/enfocus-switch-overview
copy_speed: No dedicated Smart Mover converter launched since April 2026 was verified in the searches. There is dated competition for the migration problem: Impressed published an alternatives/migration article on 2026-06-04, while 3f8h.net currently advertises migration work across n8n, Enfocus Switch, and WoodWing Connect; the 3f8h page's launch date is unverified. These are migration guidance/services, not verified self-serve converters. Smart Mover task documentation is publicly available, so a basic inventory parser may be reproducible; validated cross-platform mappings look harder because WoodWing says there is no single replacement and fit depends on the customer's setup. Sources: https://impressed.de/news-events/news/ ; https://3f8h.net/en/stories/woodwing-smart-mover-eol-migration/ ; https://helpcenter.woodwing.com/hc/en-us/articles/51981569765009-Smart-Mover-Transition-Support-Plan-after-end-of-life ; https://manualzz.com/doc/33379753/woodwing-9-smart-mover-user-guide
platform_risk: WoodWing controls the legacy product and recommends WoodWing Connect or partner-built replacements; it gives advice on moving flows and may credit STSP fees against its own replacement project. Replacement products also differ by hosting and workflow. If the product hosts n8n or lets customers configure automations through it, n8n says a commercial license is required; whether merely generating importable workflow files triggers that requirement is unverified and should be checked with n8n. Sources: https://helpcenter.woodwing.com/hc/en-us/articles/51981569765009-Smart-Mover-Transition-Support-Plan-after-end-of-life ; https://n8n.io/pricing/ ; https://support.n8n.io/article/can-i-use-your-license-for-my-use-case
defensible_asset: The proposed parser and validated mappings are only a possible future data asset; no parser, proprietary workflow corpus, or permission to retain customer mappings is evidenced. WoodWing says a plain description of each flow is more useful than its configuration file and that the suitable replacement varies by environment. A permissioned, anonymized library of mappings could become useful compiled data, but at launch the moat is weak; the product is also a one-time migration aid, with no demonstrated network effect or recurring switching costs. Sources: https://helpcenter.woodwing.com/hc/en-us/articles/51981569765009-Smart-Mover-Transition-Support-Plan-after-end-of-life ; https://3f8h.net/en/stories/woodwing-smart-mover-eol-migration/
build_effort: Estimated moderate for a read-only inventory/archive, high and uncertain for reliable conversion. The Smart Mover guide describes varied task types and says imported process settings need review and machine-specific paths or settings may need resetting. WoodWing says replacement flows need environment-specific mapping and design. A safe first product should inventory and explain flows, then export only narrowly validated mappings; broad automatic conversion is not evidenced as feasible. Sources: https://manualzz.com/doc/33379753/woodwing-9-smart-mover-user-guide ; https://helpcenter.woodwing.com/hc/en-us/articles/51981569765009-Smart-Mover-Transition-Support-Plan-after-end-of-life
channel: Inbound SEO for Smart Mover EOL and migration searches, an integrations-marketplace listing where accepted, and opt-in referrals through WoodWing solution partners. WoodWing describes a worldwide authorized partner network. Avoid unsolicited email, SMS, calls, and DMs; for any contextual ads, do not use tracking or behavioral retargeting without the required consent. The UK ICO says online advertising storage/access technologies require consent and notes contextual advertising is easier to align with UK privacy rules. Sources: https://www.woodwing.com/company/partners ; https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-the-use-of-storage-and-access-technologies/how-do-the-rules-apply-to-online-advertising/ ; https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/direct-marketing-guidance/plan-direct-marketing/
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified: there is no operating product or support history to establish <=5 hours/week. Bespoke mapping and customer validation could push this above the limit; that is an inference from WoodWing's description of environment-specific replacement work. Source: https://helpcenter.woodwing.com/hc/en-us/articles/51981569765009-Smart-Mover-Transition-Support-Plan-after-end-of-life
automation_reason: My unvalidated estimate is 45% of all work. Parsing, report generation, documentation, billing administration, and first-line support could be automated, but customer-specific mapping, conversion validation, exceptions, and partner or inbound sales still appear to need human judgment. WoodWing describes replacements as per-flow mapping and design, rather than a single standard migration. Source: https://helpcenter.woodwing.com/hc/en-us/articles/51981569765009-Smart-Mover-Transition-Support-Plan-after-end-of-life
moat_assessment: Survived the cheap kill-check, but deep evidence weakens the moat case. A maintained parser plus permissioned validated mappings could qualify as compiled data; that asset does not yet exist, and the public task documentation and active migration consultancies make a basic parser easier to copy. Do not count the hypothetical library as a current defensible moat. Sources: https://manualzz.com/doc/33379753/woodwing-9-smart-mover-user-guide ; https://3f8h.net/en/stories/woodwing-smart-mover-eol-migration/
desk_test: One-day, low-cost test: create a single-page inbound offer for a read-only workflow inventory report with a sample report built from public documentation, plus an opt-in form for a real anonymized export and a paid-pilot request. Publish it on a relevant marketplace or public product page and use only contextual search traffic if buying ads. Count qualified opt-ins and real sample files; do not treat clicks as purchase proof. WoodWing's own guidance says a plain flow description is more useful than the configuration file, so ask whether the report solves a real inventory problem before investing in conversion. Source: https://helpcenter.woodwing.com/hc/en-us/articles/51981569765009-Smart-Mover-Transition-Support-Plan-after-end-of-life
red_flags: No verified product revenue, active Smart Mover customer count, churn, buyer price, or payment evidence; revenue_proof is empty. The 2027 EOL date overstates urgency if read as an immediate shutdown: STSP permits existing customers to continue until 2029, with different terms for subscriptions and purchased licenses. WoodWing also offers migration advice and fee credit toward its own replacement work. A full converter does not currently clear the stated operating constraint: estimated automation is 45%, and <=5 owner hours/week is unverified. Sources: https://helpcenter.woodwing.com/hc/en-us/articles/51981569765009-Smart-Mover-Transition-Support-Plan-after-end-of-life ; https://www.woodwing.com/company/ ; https://3f8h.net/en/stories/woodwing-smart-mover-eol-migration/
